messages:
anya: Quick sync — proposing an RBAC tightening for the BYOK import path. Current issue: engineers in dev can trigger imports into the HSM test fleet. We need separation of duties + immutable audit events.
sam: +1, we should split the import action into two roles: importer.requester and importer.witness. Requester starts the import, witness approves. No single person can complete.
maria: Agree. Also need to make sure all import events emit an audit log with the key fingerprint, operator IDs, and the KMS wrap metadata. Retention for those logs needs to be at least 7 years for some customers.
leo: On retention, remember storage costs. Can we tier by customer SLA? e.g., default 90 days, enterprise 7 years. Also need to redact ephemeral metadata but keep provable hash.
anya: Yes SLA tiers. Implementation notes: audit event schema should include: operation, requester_id, witness_id, hsm_serial, key_fingerprint (sha256), wrap_key_id, customer_id, policy_version. Also include waveform of actions for replay.
sam: Pasting a draft policy snippet for the RBAC binding:
```yaml
roles:
  - name: importer.requester
    permissions:
      - hsm.import.create
      - hsm.import.request_metadata:view
  - name: importer.witness
    permissions:
      - hsm.import.approve
      - hsm.import.request_metadata:view
```
maria: For KMS integration, how do we record the wrap_key provenance? We should store the wrap_key_id and the KMS region + key_version. If customers use external KMS, include an attestation URL or signed statement.
leo: For external KMS, the attestation will be an additional artifact stored in the audit log S3. Could be large for some vendors, so store a checksum + S3 pointer.
anya: Ops question: when an import fails mid-protocol due to HSM firmware mismatch, what's our triage path? We had a near-miss last month.
sam: Triage path idea: 1) isolate HSM console, 2) gather import audit event + HSM console logs, 3) escalate to hw-team, 4) run rewrap test on a non-customer key. We should have a runbook attached.
maria: Can ops-bot remind us to rotate importer.witness keys monthly and log the rotation events?
ops-bot: scheduled_reminder: "Rotate importer.witness key material for PROD HSMs on the first business day of every month" :bell:
leo: Vulnerability note: vendor published firmware CVE-2025-XY1 affecting TPM handshake in some models. We need to add a vulnerability gating check before any import: HSM firmware must be in the allowed list.
anya: Good catch. Add a preflight that verifies `firmware_version in allowlist` and that `attestation_payload` signature verifies against vendor root. If mismatch, block import and notify security.
sam: Also add automated alerting to the incident channel when preflight fails more than 3 times for the same HSM within 24h. That usually indicates flakiness or targeted attack.
maria: One more: encryption-at-rest for audit logs — use a customer-specific envelope key (CEK) where customers can opt to BYOK their audit logs. That ties into Private deployment offering.
leo: Implementation constraint: if customer BYOKs audit CEK, we can't provide full-text search on those logs unless we do tokenization or allow-search proxy (with explicit consent). Flagging as privacy tradeoff.
anya: Action items: (1) sam to draft the RBAC binding PR + unit tests (due EOD Wed), (2) maria to update audit schema + retention config (due Fri), (3) leo to add firmware allowlist check to preflight and hook alerts (due Thu), (4) ops-bot to add monthly rotate reminder (done).
sam: I'll open PR and ping @maria and @leo.
maria: I'll sketch the schema now and drop a short spec in #eng-security-docs.
ops-bot: note: playbook created — https://wiki.redwood.ai/playbooks/byok-import-separation-of-duties (auto-generated entry).
leo: If anyone wants to run a tabletop for this, I can coordinate a 45m session next week.
anya: Thanks team. If no objections, we'll land the RBAC change after a 48h watch on staging logs. :thumbsup:
